o1.biggest_strength: A clean, submittable template set with a sensible tiered confirm-or-hold flow. It also has practical ops ideas: quiet hours, a holdout, and moving one agent to a 2 pm to midnight shift to cover the evening chat wave.
o1.biggest_mistake: The prepaid nudge has no incentive and is not tiered, so Tier 3 gets the same soft ask as metros. Labelling a pay-online nudge as Utility risks Meta recategorising it.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a tiered prepaid incentive or COD advance for Tier 3, backed by the per-tier loss math. Use bolder Snitch voice in the scripts. Add a net-savings metric to the scorecard.

o2.biggest_strength: Ties every tier decision to money: expected RTO loss per order is ₹70, ₹41 and ₹27, the ₹40 and ₹20 discounts sit below that loss, and calls go only to Tier 3 because only 4 agents carry chat. It adds holdouts, a net-saving metric and a tested ₹99 advance option.
o2.biggest_mistake: T1 states an expected delivery date in the confirmation, which edges toward the date promises I want to avoid. It also misses fixing the 8 pm to midnight staffing gap with a shift change.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop the date from T1. Add an evening agent shift. Give the scripts and templates a bit more Snitch punch.

reason: Both are usable, but Output 2 does the money math per pincode tier and gives Tier 3 calls, discounts and a ₹99 advance test with holdouts. That is exactly the targeted thinking I wanted. Output 1 is solid but treats the prepaid nudge the same for everyone.
